tools.description: Use for official daily settlement prices of the Fed Funds or SOFR futures strip, or any CME futures product.
Use for the probabilities of a specific meeting (take latest) or for how they evolved over time. Meeting dates come from fedwatch_meetings.
Use for the SOFR benchmark levels alongside FedWatch probabilities.
What is being published right now across the market, with no ticker or topic filter.
Use for liquidity and positioning in the Fed Funds or SOFR futures contracts FedWatch is derived from.
Use for the current futures strip behind FedWatch (product 305, 30 Day Fed Funds) or any other CME futures product id from product_search.
Start here for market-implied probabilities of the next FOMC rate decision and the list of meeting dates to pass to fedwatch_probability_history.

Currencies, Treasury and SOFR futures, equity index futures, VIX: who is long the dollar, how short leveraged funds are in ten-year notes, how asset managers are positioned in S&P futures. Leveraged funds is the hedge-fund column; asset managers is pensions, insurers and mutual funds.

Physical commodities - agriculture, energy, metals - when the question is which kind of participant is positioned, not just speculator versus hedger: managed money is the fund positioning most reports quote, swap dealers carry the index-fund flow, producers and merchants are the physical hedge. Financial futures are not here; use the financial report.

The report most commentary means by 'the COT': speculators versus hedgers, futures positions only, back to 1986 for every market. Filter by `cftc_contract_market_code` or `commodity_name` and order by `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd DESC` for the latest week. Use legacy/combined when options positions matter, and the disaggregated or financial report when the two-way speculator/hedger split is too coarse.
